test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 22 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Match the following columns on Apparatus and Purpose.
 
 Column A Column B 
 A. Litmus paper 1. To detect acidic or basic nature 
 B. Watch-glass 2. To place drops of test solutions 
 C. Test tube 3. To hold and mix solutions safely 
 D. Indicator solution 4. Shows colour change to identify acid or base </table
solution:
The correct answer is __**A-1; B-2; C-3; D-4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Litmus paper (A - 1):**
 
 
• **Litmus paper** is the most common **natural indicator** used in laboratories to **detect the acidic or basic nature** of a substance.
 
• It is extracted from **lichens** and is available as **red** or **blue** strips. **Blue litmus** turns **red** under **acidic conditions**, while **red litmus** turns **blue** under **alkaline (basic) conditions**. ***Hence, the match A-1 is correct.***
 
 
 
• **Watch-glass (B - 2):**
 
 
• A **watch-glass** is a **circular concave** piece of glass used in **chemistry** for various purposes such as **evaporating** a liquid or holding **small samples**.
 
• In the context of testing pH, it is frequently used to **place drops of test solutions** before adding an **indicator** or touching it with **litmus paper** to observe reactions. ***Hence, the match B-2 is correct.***
 
 
 
• **Test tube (C - 3):**
 
 
• A **test tube** is a standard piece of **laboratory glassware** consisting of a finger-like length of **glass** or clear plastic tubing, open at the top and closed at the bottom.
 
• Its primary function is to **hold, mix, or heat** small quantities of **solid or liquid solutions** safely during an **experiment**. ***Hence, the match C-3 is correct.***
 
 
 
• **Indicator solution (D - 4):**
 
 
• An **indicator solution** is a chemical substance that **shows a distinct colour change** when it comes into contact with an **acid** or a **base**.
 
• Common examples include **Phenolphthalein**, which remains **colourless** in **acid** but turns **pink** in **base**, and **Methyl Orange**. ***Hence, the match D-4 is correct.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Acids and Bases:**
 
 
• **Acids** are substances that have a **sour taste** and release **Hydrogen ions (H+)** in **aqueous solutions**. Their **pH value** is always **less than 7**.
 
• **Bases** are substances that are **bitter** to taste, **soapy** to touch, and release **Hydroxyl ions (OH-)**. Their **pH value** is **greater than 7**.
 
 
 
• **Natural Indicators:**
 
 
• Apart from **litmus**, other **natural indicators** include **turmeric** (which turns **red** in **base**), **China rose**, and **red cabbage** juice.
 
• These are used to identify the **chemical nature** of **household substances** without using **synthetic chemicals**.
 
 
 
• **Synthetic Indicators and pH Scale:**
 
 
• **Methyl orange** and **phenolphthalein** are **synthetic indicators** used for precise **titrations** in a **laboratory**.
 
• The **pH scale** was developed by **S.P.L. Sorensen** in **1909** to measure the **strength** of **acidity** or **alkalinity** on a scale of **0 to 14**.
 
 
 
• **Laboratory Apparatus Maintenance:**
 
 
• **Test tubes** are often made of **borosilicate glass** (like **Pyrex**) to withstand high **temperatures** and minimize **thermal expansion**.
 
• **Watch-glasses** must be thoroughly **cleaned** and **dried** to avoid **contamination** of the **test solutions** during **qualitative analysis**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Safety Protocols:** When using a **test tube** for **heating**, always use a **test tube holder** and point the mouth of the tube **away** from yourself and others to prevent injury from **spurting liquids**.
 
• **Universal Indicator:** This is a **mixture of indicators** that shows **different colours** at different **pH values** across the entire **pH scale**, providing a more **accurate measurement** than simple **litmus paper**.
 
• **Neutralization:** When an **acid** and a **base** react in a **test tube**, they form **salt and water**, a process known as **neutralization**, which often releases **heat (exothermic)**.
